questions.question: A business must register as a VAT vendor once its taxable turnover in a year passes:
options: R1 million
R10 million

questions.question: A table is priced at R2 300 INCLUSIVE of VAT. The VAT inside that price is:
options: R345 — fifteen percent of R2 300
R300 — R2 300 times fifteen over one hundred and fifteen

questions.question: The vendor pays SARS the difference between output and input tax, which taxes exactly:
options: The vendor's net profit
The vendor's total sales
The value the vendor added — hence the tax's name
The vendor's purchases

questions.question: The difference between zero-rated and exempt supplies is that:
options: Zero-rated goods carry hidden VAT; exempt goods do not
They are two names for the same treatment
Exempt suppliers charge output tax at zero percent
Zero-rated is inside the system at zero percent with input claims allowed; exempt stands outside the system with no input claims

subtopics.title: Output Less Input — the Amount Owed to SARS

questions.question: Customers returned goods worth R20 000 exclusive against credit notes. The effect on the VAT computation is:
options: Output tax falls by R3 000
Input tax falls by R3 000
Output tax rises by R3 000
No effect until the goods are resold

questions.question: The owner took stock costing R6 000 exclusive for personal use. The adjustment is:
options: Input tax increases by R900
VAT of R900 is charged back, increasing the amount owed — input credit belongs only to goods used for taxable sales
Output tax falls by R900
No adjustment, because drawings are not sales

questions.question: Bad debts of R9 200 INCLUSIVE are written off. The VAT relief is:
options: R1 380 — fifteen percent of R9 200
R1 200 — R9 200 times fifteen over one hundred and fifteen, because the debt included VAT
Nothing, since the sale already happened

questions.question: Jabulani's period: output 69 000 less 3 000 returns plus 900 drawings; input 48 000 plus 1 200 bad debts. The amount payable to SARS is:
options: R17 700 — and if input exceeded output, the difference would flip to a refund receivable

questions.question: The credit side of the VAT control account gathers:
options: Everything owed TO SARS — output tax on sales and the drawings adjustment
Input tax and payments to SARS
Only bank payments
Bad debt relief and returns

questions.question: A payment made to SARS during the period is recorded as:
options: Credit VAT Control, debit Bank
Debit VAT Control, credit Bank — the payment settles part of the slate
Debit SARS Income Tax, credit Bank
No entry until the next return is filed

questions.question: A debit balance on the VAT control account means:
options: VAT is owed to SARS as a current liability
The account contains an error
A refund is due from SARS — a current asset
Output tax was forgotten

questions.question: Input tax may only be claimed against:
options: A till slip of any kind
The owner's sworn statement
A bank statement entry
A valid tax invoice showing the supplier's VAT registration number — no invoice, no claim

subtopics.title: Ethics, Fraud and the Vendor's Duty

questions.question: VAT collected from customers is best described as:
options: Money held in trust for SARS from the moment of sale — never the vendor's own
Business income until the return is filed
A loan from SARS to the vendor
Part of gross profit

questions.question: Ringing cash sales outside the books understates:
options: Input tax
Output tax — stealing from the fiscus sale by sale
The bank balance
Drawings

questions.question: Claiming VAT on invoices from ghost suppliers is:
options: A timing difference
Legal if amounts are small
Inflating input tax — a direct extraction of money from SARS
Only a problem for the supplier

questions.question: An accountant instructed by an employer to prepare a false VAT return must:
options: Comply, since instructions come from the employer
File it but keep a private note
Adjust it slightly to reduce the lie
Refuse — assisting evasion makes the accountant party to the crime, whatever the seniority of the voice instructing

subtopics.title: The Fifteen Cents That Was Never Yours

questions.question: In the R23 washing powder sale, the R3 of VAT:
options: Belongs to SARS from the first second — MaDlamini merely holds it in passing
Belongs to MaDlamini until payday
Is MaDlamini's profit margin
Is shared between the shop and SARS

questions.question: A price tag reads R200 BEFORE VAT. The shelf price is:
options: R230 — fifteen percent added gives R30 of tax

questions.question: Taking fifteen percent of a SHELF price is wrong because:
options: Shelf prices change too often
VAT is calculated only monthly
The tax is already inside that number — taxing the tax gives the wrong answer
Fifteen percent applies only to luxury goods

questions.question: MaDlamini's brown bread against her backroom flat's rent illustrates:
options: Both carry fifteen percent VAT
Bread is exempt and rent is zero-rated
Both are outside the VAT system
Bread is zero-rated — in the system at a rate of nothing; residential rent is exempt — it never entered the building

subtopics.title: Collected In, Paid Out, and What Remains

questions.question: MaDlamini collected R6 900 of VAT on sales and paid R4 800 of VAT on purchases. She owes SARS:
The R2 100 owed equals fifteen percent of R14 000, which is:
options: Her total sales
The value she added — bought for 32 000, sold for 46 000
Her profit after expenses
Her stock on hand

questions.question: The three nudges move the bill as follows:
options: Returns up, drawings down, bad debts up
All three increase the bill
Returns down, drawings up, bad debts down
All three decrease the bill

questions.question: If a big fridge purchase makes VAT paid outweigh VAT collected for the period:
options: The excess is lost
The shop must close the period early
The fridge's VAT may not be claimed
SARS owes the refund — the slate points both ways

subtopics.title: Why Cheating VAT Is Stealing Twice

questions.question: The two-till trick is called stealing twice because it takes:
options: From SARS, and from everyone who depends on what VAT funds — clinics, schools and grants
From the customer and the supplier
From the bank and the wholesaler
From the till and the safe

questions.question: Charging customers fifteen percent without being a registered vendor is:
options: Allowed for small shops
Collecting a tax with no intention of delivering it — the aggravated version of the fraud
A minor administrative slip
Legal if prices are rounded down

questions.question: A shop buying R32 000 of stock but declaring R15 000 of sales is caught because:
options: Customers report the shop
The till breaks down eventually
The supplier's own VAT return shows every invoice issued to the shop — the mismatch is a red light on a screen
SARS counts the stock physically each month

questions.question: The examination-ready summary of VAT ethics is:
options: VAT is a cost of doing business, minimised where possible
Evasion is acceptable below the audit threshold
Only registered vendors owe ethical duties
VAT collected is held in trust for SARS; evasion is theft from the state and the public; honest tills, valid invoices and reconciled returns protect both the business and the country
